jobs.title: Hardware Engineer, DFT
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Hybrid: 3 days a week in the office, in Mountain View, New York or London. As a Design-for-Test (DFT) Engineer at Normal, you will own the DFT architecture and implementation for our next-generation, physics-inspired ASICs, from early RTL design through tapeout and silicon bring-up. You will define and drive scan/ATPG, memory built-in self-test (MBIST), and boundary-scan strategies, working closely with RTL, verification, physical design, and silicon product engineering teams. This is a hands-on technical leadership role with end-to-end ownership of silicon testability. You will establish DFT methodologies, guide external implementation partners, and ensure our designs are ready for manufacturing test. You’ll work on unconventional computing architectures where testability must be considered from the beginning, with the opportunity to shape the DFT infrastructure for an entirely new class of silicon. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - DFT Architecture: Define and own chip-level DFT architecture, including scan insertion, ATPG, scan compression, MBIST, boundary scan/JTAG, and test access infrastructure. - Implementation & Integration: Drive DFT insertion and integration across RTL, synthesis, and physical design, ensuring testability requirements are met without compromising power, performance, or area. - Test Coverage & Signoff: Own DFT verification, ATPG pattern generation, fault coverage analysis, test-mode validation, and DFT signoff through tapeout. - Manufacturing Test Readine

jobs.title: Firmware Engineer
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Hybrid: 3 days a week in the office, in Mountain View, New York or London. As a Firmware Engineer at Normal, you will create low-level software to run on our SOC to provide an interface between our physics-inspired ASICs and higher software levels. You will have to develop code that runs on a microcontroller that provides an API layer for upper software levels to exercise our AI acceleration hardware. You will interface with the hardware and software design teams, understanding both the hardware and software architectures. You will debug in various prototyping and ASIC environments. For this role, you also have to specify and create the development environment. The through-line is your firmware expertise, applied to silicon and software stacks that compute differently from anything you have coded for before. This is a seat for a firmware engineer who wants their craft to compound rather than repeat. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Development of firmware for an embedded processor on an SOC: Create firmware to support an API that bridges higher-level software to the hardware layer. - Work with software and hardware: Collaborate with software and hardware engineers to understand and specify the API requirements. - Creation of the development environment: Acquire and configure appropriate tools to create the firmware, including compilers, simulators, and debuggers. Work across multiple development environments including software simulation, RTL simulation, and physical hardware. -

jobs.title: Simulator & Debug Tools Lead
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. Nothing off the shelf simulates it, so the tool our compiler and hardware teams depend on to validate their work before silicon exists has to be built, not bought. As our Simulator & Debug Tools Lead, you will own that simulator, along with the debugging and profiling tools that integrate with our compiler. Fidelity, speed, and tooling all compete for the same hours, and you will decide where those hours go, keeping the rest of the team honest about what the chip can actually do. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Simulator Architecture: Own the architecture and roadmap of our hardware simulator, including accuracy, performance, and coverage of new hardware features as they land. Success means compiler and runtime work never waits on hardware. - Behavioral Correctness: Make the simulator's behavior, state, and memory semantics trustworthy enough that compiler and runtime engineers can act on what it tells them. - Debug and Profiling Tools: Build the debuggers, tracers, and profilers engineers actually reach for, measured by how quickly the team can find and fix a bug. - Hardware Correlation: Partner with our Design Verification and bring-up teams to correlate the simulator with RTL, FPGA prototypes, and eventually silicon, and close the loop when they disagree

jobs.title: Compiler Frontend Engineer
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. Our compiler is how models reach that hardware, and new LLM architectures show up faster than most compilers can track. A new attention variant, MoE routing scheme, or quantization approach has to be represented faithfully in our compiler before it can run, let alone run fast. As a Compiler Engineer focused on frontend and model bring-up, you will extend our IR, ops, and lowering passes so new LLM architectures are supported before a customer asks for them. This is a research-adjacent seat: you are expected to follow the literature closely, and publish on behalf of Normal. Our chip is pre-silicon, so you will validate bring-up against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, so that models are ready to run when silicon arrives. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Model Bring-up: Bring up frontend and mid-level support for new LLM architectures in our compiler, from attention variants to MoE routing schemes. Success means new architectures run correctly on our stack soon after release, ahead of customer demand. - IR and Lowering: Extend our IR, ops, and lowering passes to represent new architectural primitives faithfully rather than approximately, with test coverage that keeps them correct as the compiler evolves. - Quantization and Numerics: Represent the quan

As the founding mechanical engineer on our hardware team, you will define the physical design of that hardware at every level of integration, from the accelerator through the server to the rack. You will help determine what fits, what can be cooled, what can be serviced, and where an existing supplier platform does the job. You report to the head of our hardware systems organization and partner with our silicon, systems, and deployment engineers, and with the external design and manufacturing partners who build to our drawings. We're looking for someone who thrives on turning a system architecture into hardware and takes pride in catching the problem before the build does. The form factor, thermal envelope, mounting, and serviceability decisions you make set the foundation for the systems Normal ships, and the hardware you define is the hardware our customers run. Candidates from OEM and ODM server teams, hyperscaler infrastructure teams, and earlier-stage hardware companies could all be well qualified for this role. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Mechanical Design: Own the electromechanical design of our inference hardware as it moves from engineering configuration to deployable product, including form factor, thermal solution and airflow, connectors and cabling, and the power and thermal envelope it has to live within.

jobs.title: AI Research Resident (Algorithms Codesign)
jobs.description_text: THE RESIDENCY PROGRAM The AI Research Residency is Normal Computing's flagship program for exceptional researchers and engineers who want to work at the frontier of AI. Residents join a small, hand-picked cohort with a dedicated research mentor, direct access to the team developing the algorithms for our in-memory inference hardware, and a clear arc from onboarding through publication. Every residency is built around two milestones that mark you as part of something bigger than a single project: a research paper co-authored with our team, and a company-wide research colloquium where you present your findings to the full Normal Computing organization. You'll leave with a body of published, presented work, and a standing as one of the earliest residents to help define what this program becomes. THIS TRACK: ALGORITHMS CODESIGN Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. This track is about the computational methods that make LLM inference run efficiently on it: rethinking how operations like attention, memory access, and long-context decoding should behave on hardware that computes inside memory, rather than adapting standard GPU kernels to a new chip. jobs.title: Product Marketing, Ecosystem Partners

jobs.title: Design Engineer

That means prototyping possible directions, contributing to our core website, and getting the details right in the browser. You’ll also build reusable components and patterns that help us ship the next project faster. You: You’re a design engineer or a frontend engineer with strong design instincts. Your work shows care for typography, layout, and the timing and feel of an interaction. You’ve shipped working websites and can point to the decisions you made along the way. About Parallel Design: We design for a web used by both people and agents, grounding our work in real code, data, and evidence. jobs.title: Research Scientist, Scaling RL
jobs.description_text: Our team brings deep expertise, genuine ownership, and a drive to push the boundaries of what's scientifically possible. ABOUT THE ROLE We're training frontier models to develop deep scientific knowledge and reasoning for scientific tasks. You’ll study how RL scales with training compute, develop better algorithms, and take ideas from controlled experiments to our largest runs like Periodic Neon https://periodic.com/news/nature-is-our-learning-environment. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Design experiments to understand how RL performance scales with compute, model size, data, and reward quality, building on work such as ScaleRL https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13786 - Develop better RL algorithms, spanning policy optimization, advantage estimation, exploration, and credit assignment for long-horizon RL tasks - Build adaptive sampling and curriculum methods that adjust task difficulty, problem selection, and the number of rollouts as models improve - Study bias and stability during RL training, including importance-sampling corrections and methods to tackle policy staleness and training–inference mismatch, as discussed here https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GH4JCdAAUYg. - Improve compute efficiency across training and inference through experiments with hyperparameters, such as length penalties, rollout counts, batch sizes, and update schedules. YOU WILL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE - Hands-on experience training LLMs with reinforcement learning - Strong attention to detail and rigorous approach

jobs.description_text: Pluralis Research works on Protocol Learning: training and serving large models in a fully decentralized way on small consumer-grade devices connected via the internet. Despite being dismissed as infeasible, we have made significant advances on this problem, most recently Agora, a permissionless run that pretrained an 8B model from scratch on consumer GPUs spread over the internet, with no single participant ever holding the full weights (tech report https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13332). While many of the core research problems have been solved, Protocol Learning unlocks a series of new challenges. For the mission in full, read A Third Path: Protocol Learning https://pluralis.ai/blog/a-third-path-protocol-learning/. Agora gave us a pretrained 8B model. Post-training is how we make it useful for agentic use-cases. But every post-training stack you've seen assumes a datacenter — synchronous rollouts, fast interconnects, trusted workers. Ours gets none of that. It has to run on consumer GPUs, and Macs spread across the public internet, training a model whose weights no single participant ever holds, with rollouts arriving from a geo-distributed inference pipeline at high latencies. Your primary role is to make RL post-training work here anyway — the algorithms and the system, end-to-end. jobs.description_text: Pluralis Research works on Protocol Learning: training and serving large models in a fully decentralized way on small consumer-grade devices connected via the internet. Despite being dismissed as infeasible, we have made significant advances on this problem, most recently Agora, a permissionless run that pretrained an 8B model from scratch on consumer GPUs spread over the internet, with no single participant ever holding the full weights (tech report https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13332). While many of the core research problems have been solved, Protocol Learning unlocks a series of new challenges. For the mission in full, read A Third Path: Protocol Learning https://pluralis.ai/blog/a-third-path-protocol-learning/. jobs.title: Research Scientist - Decentralized Training and Inference Verification
jobs.description_text: Pluralis Research works on Protocol Learning: training and serving large models in a fully decentralized way on small consumer-grade devices connected via the internet. Despite being dismissed as infeasible, we have made significant advances on this problem, most recently Agora, a permissionless run that pretrained an 8B model from scratch on consumer GPUs spread over the internet, with no single participant ever holding the full weights (tech report https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13332). While many of the core research problems have been solved, Protocol Learning unlocks a series of new challenges. For the mission in full, read A Third Path: Protocol Learning https://pluralis.ai/blog/a-third-path-protocol-learning/. Our training and inference network is trustless, and the workers are GPUs scattered across the world. Many things can go wrong in this system. An inference worker can return tokens from a cheaper model, or a highly quantized version of the one it's supposed to run. Even with the right model, it can sample with the wrong parameters. Training faces its own attacks, and Agora showed what a permissionless run deals with in practice: participants who disrupt training by dropping updates or flooding the system, free-riders who submit trivial work and collect the rewards, poisoned updates that plant backdoors, attempts to extract private data from gradients and activations, and contributors who inflate their reported work to claim rewards they didn't earn. You'll take each system from parts on a table to a setup that records clean, synchronized data at a partner site, and you'll handle both the hardware and the software along the way. Most of your week will be spent with real equipment: wiring and rewiring, bringing up new sensors, chasing calibration drift, and fixing whatever stopped recording overnight. We want someone who has run systems in real deployments and brings discipline to the work. When a rig works once, you want to know why, and you want it to work the same way at every site. You don't consider a problem closed until the data coming off the system is right. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Capture rigs: Design and bring up the hardware we record with: multi-camera arrays, head- and wrist-mounted egocentric cameras, depth/IMU/force sensor packages, and teleoperation stations such as leader-follower arms. - Calibration and time sync: Own camera intrinsics and extrinsics, hardware triggering, and clock alignment across cameras, IMUs, and encoders. If the streams don't line up, the dataset isn't usable. - Root-cause failures: When a motor stalls, a camera drops frames, a power rail sags, or a bus goes quiet, find the actual cause and fix it so it stays fixed. - Field deployments: Set up and operate systems at partner sites. jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Robotics Research
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE As our first Robotics Researcher at Sieve, you'll lead the training and evaluation of world-action models (WAMs) and 3D perception systems to understand how data shapes robot capabilities. Your work connects how we capture, curate, and label physical-world data to measurable gains in robot learning. You'll run your projects from question to answer: spot where a model falls short, decide what data might close the gap, set up the experiment, and test the result on tasks and environments the model hasn't seen. A lot of this work is in 3D. Raw multimodal and egocentric video becomes useful for robot learning only once it carries geometry, pose, and action, and you'll build the systems that add them. Simulation is a tool you'll use when it makes evaluation or augmentation cheaper, not the center of the job. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Data ablations for robot learning: Compare data sources such as egocentric human video, teleop, and robot rollouts, and vary quality, mix, embodiment, and supervision to learn which choices improve policies and world models. - World-action models: Train and post-train action-conditioned world models and policies, pushing them toward skills like following commanded actions, manipulating objects, and responding to camera motion. - 3D labeling from video: Build pipelines for depth, camera trajectories, hand/body/object pose, point tracks, and scene reconstruction, so raw footage becomes action-labeled data grounded in 3D. - Evaluation design: Lock t

jobs.description_text: Why Now Sieve is one of the most capital-efficient teams in AI, with roughly 30 people serving the world's leading AI labs across every major data modality. About the Role Physical AI runs on data that captures how the real world looks, moves, and fits together in 3D. As a perception-focused Machine Learning Engineer at Sieve, you'll build the systems that turn raw egocentric, robot, and sensor footage into the training data that robotics and world-model teams depend on. You'll bring the computer vision instincts of someone who has shipped perception for robots, devices, or autonomous vehicles, and apply them to datasets at a scale few teams ever touch. One week you might recover camera pose and scene geometry across thousands of hours of first-person video. jobs.title: Device - Software Engineer (Functional Safety)
jobs.description_text: OUR MISSION SPAN develops products that accelerate the rapid adoption of renewable energy in the home. The flagship SPAN Smart Panel is the first true evolution for the traditional home electric panel, harnessing enhanced technology for metering, monitoring, and control. An expanded product suite of intelligent, integrated solutions radically lowers the cost and complexity of energy upgrades–including solar, batteries and EVs–empowering homeowners to be active, resilient and informed players in the energy market. THE TEAM AND ROLE SPAN's Device Software team is responsible for all of the software that is physically embodied in our hardware products. The Gen3 SPAN Panel is a distributed system of STM32H5 (Arm Cortex-M33) microcontroller modules that talk over CAN, meter power in real time, and open or close relays that sit directly between the grid, the home and its solar, battery and EV equipment. When that firmware makes a decision, real current moves. We are building a dedicated Functional Safety (FuSa) firmware capability to take Gen3 firmware through certification as a Power Control System under UL 3141 and as Class B control software under UL/IEC 60730-1 Annex H. This is not a checkbox exercise: FuSa at SPAN spans how we architect and partition the firmware, how we detect faults and drive the system into defined safe states, how we test and prove coverage, and how we document and trace every safety requirement back to code.
